title: Canonical eval corpus ownership, change-gate playbook, and ACL mapping
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: We need a repeatable, auditable playbook for ownership, curation, permissioning, and versioning of the canonical evaluation corpus (the reference prompt/response bundles and gold labels) that are used to detect quality regressions when models or serving configs change. Currently multiple teams maintain ad-hoc prompt bundles; changes to infra/configs often lack traceability back to which golden corpus was evaluated. This ticket defines a ownership model, change-gate workflow, signing/versioning rules, and mapping between config/model variants and corpus snapshots so that regression alerts are actionable and rollbacks can be executed with clear provenance.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Ownership model documented: each corpus has a single steward owner and an audit log of changes.
A2: Immutable snapshot mechanism implemented: corpus snapshots are content-addressed (hash) and stored with metadata about the triggering config/model fingerprint.
A3: ACLs applied: RBAC groups (stewards, reviewers, read-only consumers) enforce who can propose, approve, and publish snapshots.

A4: Change-gate automation: any merging of a serving config or model rollout that references a corpus triggers a canary eval run and, if thresholds breach, prevents automatic rollout with clear reason and links to failing examples.
A5: UI/Console mapping: console shows which corpus snapshot is pinned to a given model/config variant and allows rollback to a previous snapshot with one-click links to the eval report.
A6: Auditability: Signed manifests (SHA + signer id) and storage paths are recorded in the central registry and surfaced in the incident playbooks and runbooks.
A7: Ownership handoff process: steward rotations and expiry reviews are scheduled and actionable from the registry.
A8: Tests: end-to-end integration test that simulates a config change, triggers the eval pipeline, and verifies gating behavior in staging.
decisions: D1: Use content-addressed snapshotting (SHA256) for immutability and quick diffing; snapshots stored in S3 with versioned paths.
D2: Signing will use KMS-backed keys managed by Security; manifests include signer, timestamp, and linked PR/CL.
D3: ACL model: map to existing org groups (eval-stewards, eval-reviewers, product-read) rather than inventing new roles.
D4: Threshold defaults: canary threshold set to 1% absolute degradation for high-severity tests, configurable per-corpus.
D5: Two-stage rollout: canary (5% traffic) + full rollout; gating enforces manual override only with documented justification.
D6: Storage lifecycle: golden snapshots retained for 2 years by default; steward can request longer retention for regulatory customers.
D7: UI will display corpus fingerprints and link to signed manifest but will not surface raw golden responses unless user has 'product-read' permission.
